data.narrative:
Caelux is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Scott Graybeal that has raised $75M to date. The target operates within a frontier-tech sector represented by 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median triangulation proved inapplicable. The Climate & Energy peer set of eight companies lacked sufficient same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier overlap to support a statistically meaningful median. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $150M when applied to the $75M raised proxy.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $128M (low) to $172M (high), centered on $150M. The median reflects the single applicable methodological result. Key uncertainties include the narrow foundation of analysis—reliance on one method rather than triangulation across multiple approaches—and the absence of sufficiently comparable private peers in stage and tier. Validation would benefit from additional data on exit multiples and revenue/burn metrics within the Climate & Energy frontier-tech segment.
